newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Minero Peru to restart sell-offs in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Minero Peru to restart sell-offs in Feb.

text.p: Peruvian state miner, Minero Peru, said Friday it would restart its privatization process with the auction of the Bayover phosphate deposit in February.
The company said in a statement it would receive offers for the deposit, in Piura department, on February 11.

Minero Peru officials also confirmed plans to sell the Michiquillay copper and gold deposit, in Cajamarca department, and the Winicocha gold deposit, in Cuzco department, in the first quarter of 1997.
In the second half of 1997, the company, which began privatizing in 1993, will offer its Las Bambas copper deposit in Apurimac department and its anthricate coal deposit in La Libertad department.
The Minero Peru sales will run parallel to the ongoing, piecemeal privatization of the government's operating mining company, Centromin.
While Centromin's privatization program includes operating assets as well as deposits, Minero Peru will only sell off deposits, according to Centromin spokesman Enrique Olivares.
